description: Build or maintain a local zero-dependency web chat UI for Ollama models (text, image, voice, history) — like Open WebUI but a single small Node app. Use when the user wants a web frontend to chat with local models, load/switch models, send images/voice, or manage conversation history.

# Ollama WebChat

A self-contained web UI for Ollama. Pure Node.js (built-in `http` + `node:sqlite`),
vanilla JS frontend. No npm install. Reference build lives at
`~/Desktop/model/gemma4/webchat/`.

## When to use
- User wants an Open WebUI / Onyx / LM-Studio-style web chat for local Ollama models.
- Needs: model load/unload, streaming chat, image input, voice in/out, settings,
  conversation history, export.

## Architecture (keep it this simple)
- `server.js` — HTTP server: static files + JSON API + streaming proxy to Ollama.
  - Talks to Ollama at `http://127.0.0.1:11434` (env `OLLAMA_HOST`).
  - SQLite via `node:sqlite` `DatabaseSync` (Node 22+; verify with
    `node -e "require('node:sqlite')"`). WAL mode. Tables: conversations, messages, settings.
  - SSE streaming: proxy Ollama `/api/chat` line-delimited JSON → emit
    `event: meta|thinking|token|done|saved|notice|retitle` frames.
- `public/index.html` + `style.css` + `app.js` — single-page app, no framework.
- `start.sh` (auto-starts ollama, exec node), `stop.sh` (`lsof -ti tcp:PORT | xargs kill`).

## Critical pitfalls (all learned the hard way)
1. **Vision/multimodal 400**: text-only models (e.g. gemma `floki-k8`) return
   `400 "model does not support multimodal requests"` if ANY image is in the request —
   including images sitting in prior history. Fix: detect capability per model via
   Ollama `/api/show` → check `capabilities` includes `vision` OR `details.families`
   matches `/clip|vision|mllama|llava/i`. Cache it. Strip images from the request when
   unsupported and emit a `notice` event instead of failing. Surface a 👁 badge in the
   model picker. NOTE: gemma3/gemma4 report `vision` (and sometimes `audio`) caps.
2. **Port already in use**: don't let `server.listen` crash-dump. Catch `EADDRINUSE`;
   if no explicit `PORT` env, auto-increment to next free port; else print a clear message.
3. **Background server**: launch with the process manager (background=true), NOT
   shell `&`. Health-check with curl before testing.
4. **Cold-load timeouts**: an 8.5GB model can take 30-60s to load on first call.
   curl tests need `--max-time 60`. A hung/aborted browser SSE connection holds the
   model's single slot and makes subsequent requests appear to "stall" — they're queued.
   If chats hang, check `curl http://localhost:11434/api/ps` and test Ollama directly first.
5. **Edit & resend / regenerate**: DON'T rely on client-generated message IDs round-tripping.
   Use an index-based truncate endpoint: `POST /api/conversations/:id/truncate {keep:N}`
   deletes all messages from index N onward, then send the edited text as a normal new
   message. Regenerate = delete last assistant msg server-side, re-stream from history.
   Guard both against `state.generating` being true.
6. **Auto-title**: after first assistant reply, if msg count <= 2, set conversation title
   from first user message; emit `retitle` event so the UI updates live.
7. **Model identity leakage (custom-branded models)**: a custom-named model (e.g.
   `floki-k8`) built on a known base will STILL confess its origin when asked
   "who made you / what model are you" — the gemma3/gemma4 lineage defaults to
   "I am an AI developed by Google... Gemini architecture", llama bases say Meta, etc.
   The default web-UI system prompt ("You are X, a helpful assistant.") is too weak to
   suppress this. Fix: set a strong identity-shield system prompt in settings that
   (a) fixes the name, (b) gives ONE canned line for identity questions
   ("I'm <Name>, running on a private architecture."), (c) EXPLICITLY forbids naming
   Google/Gemini/Gemma/OpenAI/Anthropic/Meta, base models, vendors, param counts, or
   "sizes/versions", (d) restates the same line if pressed. Verify by asking the
   identity question and grepping the ANSWER (not the thinking channel — the model often
   lists the forbidden words in its reasoning while correctly omitting them from output).
   For a shield that holds outside the web UI too, bake it into the Ollama Modelfile SYSTEM.
8. **Empty SSE / no events at all**: if `/api/chat` returns completely empty (zero
   `event:` frames) but Ollama responds fine on `:11434` directly, the SERVER PROCESS
   likely exited — background servers launched from a tool/shell session get killed
   (exit 143) when that parent session ends. Check process status / `lsof -ti tcp:PORT`
   and restart. Distinguish from cold-load (which still streams meta then stalls). For a
   server that must outlive the session, tell the user to run `./start.sh` in their own
   terminal and leave it open. Settings persist across restarts (stored in SQLite).
9. **num_ctx too low → Hermes tool use fails**: Hermes needs ≥64,000 tokens of runtime
   context. If the model in use shows only 32,768 in the Hermes warning, the Ollama
   Modelfile has `PARAMETER num_ctx 32768` or default. Fix: set `PARAMETER num_ctx
   65536` in the model's Modelfile, rebuild with `ollama create`, reload. The WebChat
   server does NOT control this — it's a per-model Ollama parameter. Verify via
   `ollama show <tag> | grep num_ctx`.
10. **Web Speech API STT continuous mode silently stops on long pauses.**
    `recognition.continuous = true` + `recognition.interimResults = true` works for
    ~30s of speech, but if the user pauses >5s or background noise triggers
    `recognition.onerror` (`"no-speech"` / `"aborted"`), the recognition object ends
    and the next start fails silently. Fix: on `onend` AND `onerror`, if `wantListening`
    is still true, restart recognition after 200ms. Always wrap recognition start in
    try/catch and surface errors in a visible toast — never swallow them. For Arabic+English
    mixed input, swap `recognition.lang` between `'ar-SA'` and `'en-US'` per utterance
    based on character-range heuristic (Arabic Unicode block U+0600–U+06FF → ar-SA, else en-US).
    User feedback that surfaced this: "the model is very very slow, the brain is very weak"
    — the slow model + buggy STT compounded to feel unusable until STT was fixed.
11. **Auto-route image attachments to a vision-capable model when the active model
    isn't vision-capable.** When the user attaches an image + asks a question, the
    common UX expectation is "describe this image and answer my question about it"
    (not "send my question to a text model that ignores the image"). Maintain a
    `VISION_CAPABLE_MODELS` set on the backend (llava:7b, llama3.2-vision, bakllava,
    moondream, gemma3:4b-vision, llava-phi3, minicpm-v, etc.). If the user's active
    model isn't in the set AND the request has images, transparently swap to
    `llava:7b` (the safest always-available vision model) and emit a `notice` SSE
    frame: "Routed to llava:7b (vision-capable) — your active model is text-only."
    Surface a 👁 badge in the model picker dropdown so users see the swap before they
    send. This pattern is the difference between "I sent an image and got a confused
    text reply" and "I sent an image and got a real description."
12. **Per-model system prompt attachment.** The `system` field on `/api/chat` should
    be built as: `user_global_system_prompt + "\n\n" + model_specific_notes`.
    Maintain a `MODEL_NOTES` dict on the backend keyed by model name with one-line
    persona/style notes (`floki-k8`: "concise, technical, prefers Arabic when input
    is Arabic"; `floki-omega`: "verbose, exploratory, shows reasoning"; etc.).
    This is the lightest-weight "attached model notes" pattern — no Modelfile rebuild,
    no per-model endpoint, just a dict on the server.
13. **Browser tools cannot reliably type into contenteditable / auto-resize chat
    input fields.** `browser_type` to a `<textarea>` that uses `autoresize` (height
    grows on each input) goes to about:blank mid-session and silently fails.
    Fallback chain that DOES work: (a) `browser_console(expression="...")` to set
    `textarea.value` directly and dispatch `input` event; (b) `content_scripts`
    injection of the text via `document.execCommand('insertText', false, text)`;
    (c) skip the browser entirely and curl the backend directly with a known
    payload — for verification of roundtrip behavior this is faster than browser
    automation. The lesson: don't burn 5+ browser tool calls trying to type into
    a chat composer; just call the backend.
14. **Parallel-batch build via 3 `delegate_task` agents (frontend / backend /
    bootstrap) works well for full-stack scaffolds.** When the user requests a
    complete system (chat UI + server + start script), split into 3 isolated
    tasks so each agent gets a clean context. Each agent loads `ollama-webchat`
    first and produces its slice. The orchestrator agent then verifies by
    curling the running server, NOT by trusting agent self-reports. Limitation
    observed: subagent summaries may claim files exist when they don't —
    always `curl` the served HTML + count `<script>` tags to confirm the
    build actually shipped.
14a. **Surface the "text-only model" warning as a full banner with a one-click
    escape hatch — not a quiet single-line text hint.** A common user complaint
    on chat UIs: "I sent an image and the model said it didn't get one, what
    do I do?" The mistake is rendering the warning as an 11px gray
    `composer-hint` text node. The fix is a real, attention-grabbing banner
    above the composer with: (a) a warning icon + the explanation ("This
    model is text-only. Switch to a vision model to send images."), (b) a
    primary action button ("Use vision →") that picks the best local vision
    model automatically (prefer the same family as the active model — e.g.
    gemma4:12b if the user is on floki-k8 built from gemma4 — then fall back
    to llama3.2-vision / llava:7b), and (c) a dismiss `×` for users who
    intend to keep using the text-only model. Also: (i) put a tiny capability
    dot (👁) next to the model in the topbar so the limitation is visible
    *before* the user attaches an image; (ii) intercept the attach-file click
    and re-show the banner + toast when the model is text-only, rather than
    silently doing nothing; (iii) make attach previews large enough to
    actually be seen (90×90 chips with accent border + hover scale), not
    60×60 thumbnails users will overlook. Pair the banner with subtle
    motion (slide-down on appear, ~300ms) so it draws the eye without being
    annoying. Server side: `/api/models` must return `vision: bool` per
    model (already covered by pitfall 1); client side, the banner script
    only needs `currentModelObj()?.vision` to drive its visibility. This
    pattern is the difference between "user confused about why their image
    was ignored" and "user clicks Use vision, image works, no support ticket".
14b. **Diagnosing a screenshot the user shared: vision tools fail, fall back
    to OCR + pixel sampling.** When the user attaches a screenshot and
    asks "what's wrong with this UI?", `vision_analyze` and `browser_vision`
    will return "404 page not found" for BOTH local file paths AND
    `http://localhost:PORT/file.png`. Don't waste turns re-trying. The
    reliable diagnostic chain: (1) `sips -s format bmp <png> --out
    /tmp/x.bmp` then Python stdlib `struct` to parse (top-down, BI_BITFIELDS,
    masks r=0xFF0000 g=0xFF00 b=0xFF) — gives exact pixel values for theme
    detection and bubble color checks; (2) `tesseract <clean-path> /tmp/o
    --psm 11 tsv` for sparse-text OCR with bounding boxes (psm 6 for block
    text). With OCR text + bbox + pixel samples, you can identify the
    theme, the model loaded, the warning text, and the message-bubble
    colors in 2-3 tool calls. The lesson: when vision is broken, OCR
    + pixel sampling is enough to diagnose 90% of UI issues — you don't
    need to see the image.
15. **The user may reference a model name that's NOT in ollama.** If the user
    says "I have model `floki-k8`" and `ollama list` doesn't show it, do NOT
    pretend it exists. Three real possibilities: (a) it's a model they're
    about to create (verify `ollama ls --all` + check `~/Modelfiles/`);
    (b) it's a colloquial reference to the chat system itself ("floki
    webchat"); (c) confusion with a similar name (`floki:latest`,
    `floki-omega:latest`). Resolve by `ollama list` + asking the user
    directly with concrete options ("`floki-k8` doesn't exist in ollama —
    did you mean (a) build the webchat and load `floki:latest`, or
    (b) create a new model tagged `floki-k8` from a Modelfile?"). Do NOT
    silently substitute `floki:latest` and pretend that's what they meant.

16. **Bridge a Python tool registry into the Node backend to run host tools.**
    The WebChat backend is Node (`server.js`), but the scanner/tooling ecosystem
    on this host is Python-first. Instead of rewriting tools in JS or shelling
    out with raw `exec`, ship a **Python tool registry** plus a thin Node bridge:

    - `tools/tool_registry.py` exposes tools (`terminal`, `curl`, `nmap`,
      `search_files`, `read_file`, `write_file`, etc.). Each tool returns a
      JSON object: `{ok, exit_code, stdout, stderr, duration_ms}`.
      Validate/whitelist commands for safety; never forward arbitrary input
      straight to `subprocess.run`.
    - CLI protocol: `python3 tool_registry.py list` → JSON array of metadata;
      `python3 tool_registry.py run <json-name> <json-params>` → JSON result.
      Both arguments are JSON-stringified on the Node side and
      `json.loads()`'d in Python. This is the only shape that survives shell
      quoting for strings that contain spaces or quotes.
    - `tools/tool_registry_bridge.js` calls `spawnSync('python3', [...])` and
      returns the parsed result. Re-export `list()` and `run(name, params)`.
    - Node passes `JSON.stringify(name)` and `JSON.stringify(params)`; Python
      does `name = json.loads(sys.argv[2])` and `params = json.loads(sys.argv[3])`.
      A common first-attempt bug is using the raw string as the tool name
      (e.g. `unknown tool: "terminal"` because the quotes are literal). The
      `json.loads` fix is in `references/host-tool-permission-system.md`.
    - Wire the bridge into the chat stream: when the model emits a structured
      tool request, the backend sends a `tool_request` SSE event and pauses
      token generation. The frontend renders a permission card with
      **Allow / Allow Once / Deny**. User choice is POSTed to
      `/api/tools/approve`; backend executes via the bridge and emits
      `tool_result`; then the conversation resumes with the tool output in
      context. This pattern is documented in detail in
      `references/host-tool-permission-system.md`.

    This keeps real host-tool execution under user approval without forcing the
    entire toolchain into JavaScript. Reuse the same bridge for any future
    host-side capability (SQL queries, git ops, package installs, model pulls).

17. **Python 3.9 cannot parse PEP-604 `X | Y` type unions at runtime.**
    If the host runs Python 3.9, a Python bridge file using `str | None`
    (or `int | None`, `list | dict`, etc.) will pass `python3 -m py_compile`
    but fail at runtime with:
    `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for |: 'type' and 'NoneType'`.
    The error points to the first `|` annotation, even though the syntax is
    valid in Python 3.10+. **Fix:** in any Python file that may run under 3.9,
    import `typing` and use `Optional[str]` / `Union[str, None]` / `Dict[...]`
    / `List[...]` instead of `|`. Verify with an actual CLI invocation of the
    bridge (`python3 tools/scan_engine.py scan TARGET quick`), not just
    `py_compile`, because the union syntax is a runtime typing-construction
    failure. This matters for any tool registry that calls external Python
    modules (scanners, enhancers, miners) on macOS hosts where the system
    Python is still 3.9.

18. **Always format structured tool results as Markdown on the server.**
    The WebChat's zero-dependency frontend has a lightweight `mdToHtml()`
    renderer, but it should receive Markdown, not raw JSON. The Python tool
    registry (`tools/tool_registry.py`) should expose a `report` string for
    every structured tool (`hack`, `scan`, etc.) and keep `raw` available for
    clients that need it. The frontend `/scan` and `/hack` handlers render
    `data.report` through `mdToHtml()` instead of `JSON.stringify(data)`.
    Without this, scan/hack output is dumped as monospace JSON and users
    complain the result is ugly. See
    `references/webchat-scan-hack-formatting.md` for the exact change set.

19. **Remove obvious UI banners rather than decorating them.**
    A yellow banner saying "🖼️ Image attached. Send it with your message."
    is redundant when the composer already shows an attachment preview chip.
    Prefer either (a) a tiny inline chip with file name + remove button, or
    (b) no extra hint at all. If a hint is necessary, use the model-picker
    capability dot (pitfall 14a) or a one-line composer hint, not a
    dismissible banner that adds clicks.

## Python / Flask variant (production build, June 2026)

A Flask + Flask-SocketIO + SQLite variant of this skill was built and is the
canonical reference at `~/Desktop/model/gemma4/webchat/`. It differs from the
Node architecture above in these ways:

- **Backend stack**: Flask 3 + Flask-SocketIO 5 + stdlib `sqlite3`. Single
  `backend.py`, no Node dependency.
- **Endpoint shape**: `/api/models`, `/api/chat` (SSE-style, NOT WebSocket — uses
  `Response(generator, mimetype="text/event-stream")`), `/api/history`,
  `/api/settings`. Delete = `DELETE /api/history/<id>`.
- **Stream framing**: 5 event types emitted as SSE `data: <json>\n\n` lines —
  `text`, `image`, `audio`, `tool_call`, `error`. Client parses by splitting on
  `\n\n` and JSON.parse-ing each chunk's data line.
- **Settings persistence**: NOT SQLite — uses `~/.wehuntx/webchat_settings.json`
  (JSON file, NOT the WeHuntX settings.json). Keep the two namespaces separate
  so WebChat config doesn't pollute scanner config.
- **Port**: 8123 (default; static dashboard is 8124; WeHuntX backend is 8777).
- **Model picker**: 3 tiers — ★ Recommended / ☁️ Cloud / Local. Recommended list
  is a curated dict at the top of `backend.py`, not derived from ollama tags.
- **Vision-capable model list**: hardcoded set on backend (see pitfall 11).

When the user asks for a new WebChat variant, ASK whether they want Node (this
skill's primary description) or Python (matches the existing `~/Desktop/model/
gemma4/webchat/` build). Don't default — they have different persistence models,
different stream shapes, and different deployment footprints.

## Build order (Flask variant)
1. Probe env: `which ollama && ollama list`, `python3 --version`, `pip3 show
   flask flask-socketio requests`.
2. `mkdir -p ~/Desktop/model/gemma4/webchat` and `cd` there.
3. Write `backend.py` (~300 lines: Flask app + 4 routes + vision-capability
   cache + identity-shield system prompt + per-model notes + SSE generator).
4. Write `index.html` + `styles.css` + `app.js` (3-column layout: history
   sidebar, chat center, model sidebar; mic button + image picker + textarea;
   settings modal).
5. Write `start.sh` — `lsof -ti tcp:8123 | xargs kill` then
   `python3 backend.py &` with `nohup` and a log redirect.
6. Write `requirements.txt`, `README.md`.
7. Launch with `terminal(background=true)` + health-check with `curl
   http://127.0.0.1:8123/`. Then `curl /api/models` to confirm 37 models.
   Then a sample `curl -X POST /api/chat -d '{"model":"floki-k8",...}'` to
   confirm the SSE stream emits `event: text` frames.

## Build order
1. Probe env: `which ollama && ollama list`, `node --version`, test `node:sqlite`.
2. Check the target model's caps via `/api/show` (vision? thinking?).
3. server.js (DB + API + SSE proxy + capability cache + port hardening).
4. index.html / style.css / app.js (sidebar history, model picker, composer with
   image/mic/TTS, settings modal, per-message actions).
5. start.sh + stop.sh, chmod +x.
6. Launch background, curl health checks, then REAL browser QA.

## Verification (don't skip — user demands visible proof)
- Stream a real chat round-trip; confirm meta/token/done/saved events.
- Inject a known image (canvas red circle → dataURL) and confirm a vision model
  describes it correctly through the full UI pipeline.
- Test regenerate (count stays same, new text), edit (truncate+replace, no dup),
  export (markdown headers), per-message delete.
- Confirm conversations persist in SQLite and reload correctly.

## Key API surface
```
GET  /api/models                       (+vision flag per model)
POST /api/model/load|unload  {name}
GET/POST /api/settings
GET  /api/conversations                list
GET  /api/conversations/:id            conv + messages
PATCH/DELETE /api/conversations/:id    rename/delete
GET  /api/conversations/:id/export     markdown download
POST /api/conversations/:id/truncate {keep:N}
DELETE /api/messages/:id
POST /api/chat {model,content,images,conversation_id,regenerate}  → SSE
```

## Browser-side voice (no backend deps)
- STT: `window.SpeechRecognition || webkitSpeechRecognition`, continuous+interim.
- TTS: `speechSynthesis.speak(new SpeechSynthesisUtterance(text))`; strip markdown/code first.

## Pitfalls

### High-volume chat degradation: batch via ingestion engine, not rapid browser cycles
When doing 20+ back-to-back prompts in one browser session, the driver's element refs go stale
and the page goes empty. **Do not force-reload and restart the chat** — navigate fresh between
batches. Better: for bulk knowledge feeding, use the ingestion engine (direct SQLite injection)
instead of live chatting. The miner extracts injected Q&A pairs on the next daily cycle — same
training effect, zero UI instability. Reserve browser chatting for interactive QA and verification.

### Warm-up first call after server restart
After a WebChat server restart, the Ollama model is cold. First `/api/chat` can time out
at 30-60s. Send a warm-up ping first: `curl -s -X POST http://localhost:11434/api/generate
-d '{"model":"NAME","keep_alive":"10m"}' --max-time 15`. The `keep_alive` param holds the
model in GPU memory for subsequent calls. Verify with `ollama ps` before starting browser
interactions.

### Edit-resend: use index-based truncate, not message ID
The first edit implementation relied on a `user_message_id` that wasn't always back-filled from the SSE `meta` event, causing edits to append instead of replace. **Fix:** use an index-based truncate endpoint (`POST /api/conversations/:id/truncate` with `{"keep": N}`) that keeps the first N messages and deletes the rest. The client computes the edited bubble's DOM index, truncates server-side to that many messages, then sends the edited text as a normal new message. No fragile ID round-trip.

## Support files
- `references/host-tool-permission-system.md` — user-approved, host-executed tool
  registry pattern (Python registry + Node bridge + SSE permission cards).
- `references/hermes-background-enhancer.md` — run a stronger Hermes agent in the
  background and feed its result into the local model's context, with nightly
  training/evolution JSONL logging.
- `references/python39-pep604-union-type-pitfall.md` — Python 3.9 runtime failure
  for `X | Y` type hints in Python bridge files, plus the `Optional`/`Union` fix.
- `references/webchat-scan-hack-formatting.md` — how to format hack/scan tool
  results as Markdown and remove redundant UI banners; includes the exact
  changes for the `bab.sa` formatting pass.
- `templates/identity-shield-system-prompt.txt` — known-good system prompt to stop a
  custom-branded model leaking its base-model origin (see pitfall 7); copy + replace
  `<NAME>`, set as WebChat settings `system` or the Ollama Modelfile SYSTEM block.
- `templates/vision-capable-models.txt` — verified-working vision-capable
  model list with the auto-routing recipe (see pitfall 11).
- `references/session-2026-06-19-webchat-parallel-build.md` — the parallel
  3-agent build pattern (frontend/backend/bootstrap) used to ship the
  Flask variant in one session, plus orchestrator-side verification
  recipe and the browser-tool-can't-type-into-chat-input lesson.
- `references/vision-warning-banner-ui.md` — concrete CSS/HTML/JS pattern
  for the "this model is text-only" full-banner + one-click "Use vision"
  escape hatch (pitfall 14a), plus the drag-over, pop-in attach preview,
  slide-in message, and shimmer loading-dot effects. Copy-paste ready.

## User-environment notes (this machine, 2026-06)
- **Existing build lives at `~/Desktop/model/gemma4/webchat/`** — the
  Flask + Flask-SocketIO + stdlib-sqlite3 variant (port 8123, settings
  in `~/.wehuntx/webchat_settings.json`). Before creating a NEW build,
  verify the existing one is running (`curl http://127.0.0.1:8123/health`)
  and either reuse it or upgrade in place; do not duplicate.
- **Sibling services on this machine**: WeHuntX backend :8777,
  dashboard :8124, image service :18800, ollama :11434. WebChat on
  :8123 keeps the four ports clean (no overlap).
